newsitem.title: USA: Weather more key to CBOT corn than cattle report.
newsitem.headline: Weather more key to CBOT corn than cattle report.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures were expected to draw mild support from the U.S. Agriculture Department's cattle on feed data when Project A trading opens Sunday night but weekend weather will likely overshadow the cattle placements data, analysts said.

"I'm still going to call corn lower, one to two (cents) lower," said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa. "I think they're more concerned about the weather right now and whether or not it's going to be good enough to put some more bushels on the yield."
Corn trades on CBOT's Project A overnight session from 2230 to 0430 CDT (0330 to 0930 GMT) Sunday through Thursday.

Weather forecasts called for rains ranging from 0.25 to 1.50 inches this weekend across most of the U.S. Midwest. Parts of the Midwest have been too dry for optimal crop development and crops in those areas may still benefit from rain.

USDA's Cattle on Feed Report, released Friday, showed July placements of cattle on feed in the seven leading cattle feeding states were 18 percent greater than a year earlier, at 1,756 million head, much more than analysts had expected.
That would mean more demand for corn, a primary feed ingredient in livestock rations.
Analysts said trade in the corn market would likely be cautiously quiet Sunday night and Monday in anticipation of USDA's weekly crop ratings due Monday afternoon.

"I'm sure the trade is going to want to take a look at this Monday's crop condition report before they get too wild on anything," said Doug Hjort, president of Hjort Associates. "The thinking is that we will see some (corn condition) improvement."

USDA surprised the market on Tuesday by forecasting U.S. corn production this year at 9.276 billion bushels, well below trade expectations. Traders pointed to dry weather in July as the primary cause of lost yield potential and continued dry weather could further cut production, they said.
